(a) Let us consider you pushed the stone for $2\text{ s}$, what happens then?

**Answer:** In $2\text{ s}$ the velocity of the stone will be increased to:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 0.5 \times 2\text{ m/s} = 1\text{ m/s}$$
Then the stone will move with a uniform velocity of $1\text{ m/s}$.

In $2\text{ s}$ your velocity will be:
$$u + at = 0 + 1 \times 2\text{ m/s} = 2\text{ m/s}$$
Then you will move in the reverse direction with a uniform velocity of $2\text{ m/s}$.

Earlier we have discussed gravitational force or gravity and spring force. Now we shall discuss about a totally different type of force, this is frictional force.

Let us consider a wooden piece on a table and we are trying to create an acceleration by applying a force on it. As shown in figure 3.15, we are applying a force $F$ on the mass from left to right. It will be seen that due to friction between the wooden piece and the table, a frictional force $f$ is developed on the wooden piece and this is lowering the applied force acting from right to left.

If you think that due to friction a frictional force is developed from right to left, so if I apply a force on the wooden piece from the left too, then since the applied force and the frictional force are in the same direction, I will get an extra force! But it will be seen that the frictional force is still working in the opposite

figures.caption: Figure 3.15: If a force is applied on a mass then another force may develop in the reverse direction due to friction.
figures.description: A wooden block on a table with a force F acting to the right and a frictional force f acting to the left.
